Theme

Latin word

senātus

senātus, senātūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a town council; a parliament (Neo-Latin); classically the senate; the senate; a sitting of the senate

In this lexicon

  • council

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 10.79.1; Pollio in Cic. Fam. 10.32.2 (Lewis & Short): of Gades; M-O s.v. city council

  • parliament

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. legislature, parliament

  • senate

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 19; Traupman 180; Levi–Bini p. 46

  • session

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 12.25a.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 180, 376: senate session, senātus; to hold a session, senātum habēre

  • senātus mūnicipālis: council

    modern

Examples

  • nē quis capiat magistrātum nēve sit in senātū minor annōrum trīgintā

    that no one under thirty may hold office or sit on the council (in the towns of Bithynia)Plin. Ep. 10.79.1

    In the entry for council

  • quae nisi essent in senibus, nōn summum cōnsilium majōrēs nostrī appellāssent senātum

    if these qualities were not found in old men, our ancestors would not have called their highest council the senateCic. Sen. 19

    In the entry for senate

  • senātus fidem atque ingenium puerī exōsculātur

    the senate warmly praised the boy’s loyalty and witGell. 1.23.13

    In the entry for senate

    to call (hold) a senate sessionTraupman 180

    In the entry for senate

  • senātum dīmittere

    to dismiss the senateTraupman 179

    In the entry for senate
